title: Agentic systemd Runtime and Resource Governance
purpose: Define how DUMMIE Engine uses Linux systemd, cgroups, zram, swap, journald, GPU services, and explicit lab lifecycle commands to run agent workloads only when needed and release hardware resources when the user is doing non-agent work.

contract_invariants.name: DUMMIE lab off means no DUMMIE workload
contract_invariants.rule: After dummie-lab-off, ollama.service must be inactive and no process may be running the exact DUMMIE MCP server path layers/l1_nervous/mcp_server.py.

contract_invariants.name: Hardware substrate remains available
contract_invariants.rule: dummie-lab-off must not stop asusd.service, supergfxd.service, nvidia-persistenced.service, nvidia-powerd.service, zram-config.service, journald, networking, or the desktop.

contract_invariants.name: MCP remains client-owned
contract_invariants.rule: DUMMIE MCP uses STDIO and must be launched by the MCP client through /usr/local/bin/dummie-mcp; it must not be converted into a persistent daemon unless the transport changes.

contract_invariants.name: Ollama is demand-loaded
contract_invariants.rule: Ollama may be started by dummie-lab-on or by a future resource governor before local reasoning. It must be stoppable by dummie-lab-off when the user is doing non-agent work.

contract_invariants.name: Agent workloads live in cgroups
contract_invariants.rule: Long-lived non-STDIO agents must use agentic.slice or agentic-agent@.service so CPU, memory, IO, task count, logs, and failure policy are observable and bounded.

contract_invariants.name: Zram first, disk swap last
contract_invariants.rule: zram must have higher priority than /var/lib/swapfile-agentic so pressure goes to compressed RAM before NVMe swap.

contract_invariants.name: Monitoring precedes optimization
contract_invariants.rule: Any autonomous resource optimizer must expose process, cgroup, RAM, swap, GPU, token, and idle-time signals before killing, unloading, or restarting workloads.

expected_state: no agentic-agent@*.service unless explicitly started for another task
ASUS, NVIDIA persistence, zram, and journald remain active
normal_desktop.use_case: Chrome, research, writing, desktop work, non-agent coding.

expected_state: ollama.service active but models load only on demand
long-lived agent workers run under agentic.slice
agent_lab.use_case: DUMMIE Engine orchestration, MCP gateway use, local reasoning, multi-agent experiments.

expected_state: prints RAM, swap, zram, and GPU summary
observability.use_case: Before and after experiments, debugging resource pressure, checking that lab-off released resources.

required_future_resource_governor_signal: per-cgroup memory.current, memory.high, memory.max, cpu.pressure, memory.pressure, io.pressure
GPU memory used, GPU utilization, power draw
Ollama model loaded state and idle duration
DUMMIE active sessions and event queue depth
local reasoning token estimates and actual token counts when provider metadata is available
resource release actions with reason and timestamp
required_future_actions: start ollama before local reasoning when inactive
release or stop ollama after idle timeout when no DUMMIE sessions are active
refuse to unload during an active generation or transaction
emit JSON status for dashboards and tests

runtime: systemctl is-active asusd supergfxd zram-config systemd-journald
lab_off_acceptance: Run dummie-lab-off outside active MCP sessions.
Verify systemctl is-active ollama returns inactive.
Verify pgrep -f 'DUMMIE Engine/layers/l1_nervous/mcp_server.py' returns no processes.
Verify Chrome and normal desktop work are not competing with Ollama or DUMMIE MCP.

traceability.next_spec_candidate: ResourceGovernor: event-driven Ollama lifecycle, token accounting, and cgroup-aware process optimization.
